newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Simitis election in Greece.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Simitis election in Greece.

text.p: The United States on Monday welcomed the election of socialist Costas Simitis as Greece's prime minister, saying he had shown he was a serious leader dedicated to better ties with Washington and others.

"The prime minister has proven himself to be a serious leader dedicated to improving relations with his neighbours, and to strengthening Greece's ties to the rest of Europe and the United States," State Department deputy spokesman Glynn Davies told reporters.

"Under his stewardship, Greece has taken steps to reduce inflation while increasing growth (and) he has indicated that he intends to continue to pursue those policies," Davies said. "The United States of course has had a cooperative positive relationship with Simitis and we expect that to continue."

In his short time since inheriting the mantle of the late socialist party founder Andreas Papandreou in January, Simitis has worked hard to convince the United States and the European Union that a new era in relations was at hand.

He has also vowed to turn Greece's sprawling, inefficient bureaucracy into a "hands-on" meritocracy where anyone who fails to work hard will be replaced, a no-nonsense approach that is a far cry from his predecessor.
Davies said the United States expected Simitis to "continue some of the very excellent policies that we've seen in recent months."

After succeeding the ailing Papandreou in January, the 60-year-old Simitis scored a leadership victory to run the party after Papandreou died in June and cemented his grip on power by leading the socialists to a solid election victory.
